photos.c: Mark Miles - numero uno! Two 5 kms and two wins in Gold Cup competition.
Left: Mark Miles took up the pace for most of the 'A' 1500m at Copthall before getting jumped by the pack over the last 300 metres.
Below: Ignoring the pouring rain at the end of the race. Lee Hurst, Paul Freary, Spencer Barden, Jason Lobo, Paul Evans and Mark Miles.

Belgrave's Winning AAA 12-Stage Team at Sutton Park. Back row: Andy Graffin, Spencer Barden, Paul Freary, Stephen Sharp, Alaster Stewart, David Anderson, Allen Graffin, Paul Evans. Front row: Lee Hurst, Mark Miles, Alan Mead (team manager), Richard Ward, Charles Herrington.

Above (1): Belgrave's men retained the AAA 6-Stage Road Relay Championship at Sutton Park in October 2002. Mark Miles, Richard Ward, Spencer Barden, Stephen Sharp, Allen Graffin and David Anderson celebrate keeping hold of the trophy for another year. This is the hardest team title to win - can they make it three in a row in October 2003?
Bottom left: Mark Miles took the Belgrave lead to over two minutes on stage 5.

Above: The start of the inaugural AAA 5 km Road Championship, held in conjunction with the Horwich Carnival race.  From left to right Peter Riley (107 Leigh H), Rob Whalley (90 Bristol & West AC), Andi Jones (51 Salford), David Anderson (88 Belgrave H) with Mark Miles on his left, behind Ian Mitchell (114 Tipton), the eventual winner Wilf Taragon (85 Birchfield), Mark Tucker (126 Australia), Birhan Dagne (217 Belgrave H) is on the right.  Mark Miles placed second with the fastest time run by a Briton in Britain this year – 13:58 – and took the AAA Championship.
Mark Miles staged a terrific finish in the AAA 5k to all but catch Wilf Taragon (Birchfield/Kenya)

Above: The AAA 5k Road Race was again held in Horwich. It was only the second time the Championship has been held and the Bels have medalled on each occasion – silver in 2005 and now gold in 2006. Individual AAA Champion was Chris Davies of Telford (in the red and yellow), second was Peter Riley of Leigh (white vest with green diagonal) and third was our own Mark Miles (177). Simon Jones (not pictured) and Richard Ward (181) made up the Belgrave team. The Open race was won by Birchfield, running three Africans, but they were not eligible for the AAA race.

Above: Maximum points in the 5000 metres.  At the halfway point Mark Miles was closely shadowed by John Nysaginia (Birchfield) and our own Stephen Sharp but by the end of the race the gap was 11 seconds with Stephen heading the B race by 20 seconds.

NATIONAL 6-STAGE ROAD RELAY CHAMPIONS – 2007
Yes, we’ve brought you pictures like this before – but while our lads are able to notch up such great victories, we’ll have no hesitation in bringing you further such images. Left to right: James Kelly (stage 2), Phil Wicks (6), Stephen Sharp (1), Mark Miles (5), Jonathan Blackledge (3) and Simon Jones (4)

NATIONAL CROSS COUNTRY RELAY CHAMPIONS – 2007
A third National title of the Autumn season came Belgrave’s way at the end of a riveting race at Berry Hill Park, Mansfield. It was only the second time in our history that we’ve managed to pull this one off. Left to right: Mark Pollard (stage 2), Stephen Sharp (1), Phil Wicks (4), Mark Miles (3).
